questions.question: In an office, the average salary of 22 staff members was ₹81,400. If the average salary of staff and the Vice Chairman was ₹89,600, then how much is the salary of the Vice Chairman (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average salary of 22 staff members = ₹81,400

Total staff members including Vice Chairman = 22 + 1 = 23

Average salary of 23 members = ₹89,600

**Formula Used:**

Total Salary = Average Salary x Number of Members

**Calculation:**

Total salary of 22 staff members = 81,400 x 22

Total salary of 22 staff members = 1,790,800

Total salary of 23 members = 89,600 x 23

Total salary of 23 members = 2,060,800

Salary of Vice Chairman = Total salary of 23 members - Total salary of 22 staff members

Salary of Vice Chairman = 2,060,800 - 1,790,800

Salary of Vice Chairman = 270,000

**The salary of the Vice Chairman is ₹2,70,000.**

questions.question: In an election, 750 votes were cast for the two contestants, Bharti and Manya. Bharti defeated Manya by 16% votes. If there were no invalid vote, then how many votes did Manya get?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total votes = 750

Bharti defeated Manya by 16% votes.

**Calculation:**

Let the number of votes Manya received be x.

Then, the number of votes Bharti received is (750 - x).

Since Bharti defeated Manya by 16% of the total votes, we have the equation:

(Votes of Bharti) = (Votes of Manya) + 16% of total votes

750 - x = x + (16/100) × 750

750 - x = x + 120

Now, solve for x:

750 - 120 = 2x

630 = 2x

x = 630 / 2

x = 315

**Therefore, Manya received 315 votes.**

questions.question: In a class, there are 30 boys and 20 girls. The average score of boys in Physics is 92, whereas the average score of girls in Physics is 83. Find the average score of the whole class in Physics.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Boys** to **Girls** = 30 : 20 = 3 : 2

Assume a base average of 83. Deviation for boys = 92 − 83 = +9

Total deviation = 3 × 9 = 27

Net increase in average = 27 ÷ (3 + 2) = 27 ÷ 5 = 5.4

Final Average = 83 + 5.4 = 88.4

**∴ The correct answer is 88.4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of **boys** (n₁) = 30, Average score (A₁) = 92

Number of **girls** (n₂) = 20, Average score (A₂) = 83

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/35f4ec81271da01979351256869a2ada87b899cf99f143e53bb9722e3f511f70.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Combined Average = (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total marks of **boys** = 30 × 92 = 2760

⇒ Total marks of **girls** = 20 × 83 = 1660

⇒ Total marks of the **whole class** = 2760 + 1660 = 4420

⇒ Total number of students = 30 + 20 = 50

⇒ Average score of the class = 4420 ÷ 50

⇒ Average score of the class = 88.4

**∴ The correct answer is 88.4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Concept

When two groups with different averages are combined, the resulting average is closer to the group with the **larger number of members**.

Average of Arithmetic Progression

For a set of numbers in **A.P.**, the average is simply the arithmetic mean of the first and last term: (First + Last) ÷ 2.

Effect of Constant Values

If each value in a set is increased or decreased by a constant **k**, the new average also increases or decreases by **k**.</p

questions.question: Find the HCF of 36 and 84.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

We need to find the HCF (Highest Common Factor) of 36 and 84.

**Concept used:**

We will use the prime factorization method to find the HCF.

**Calculation:**

36 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 = 2² × 3²

84 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 7 = 2² × 3 × 7

The common prime factors are 2² and 3.

HCF = 2² × 3 = 4 × 3 = 12

**Therefore, the HCF of 36 and 84 is 12.**

questions.question: In a lead pipe 4.2 m long, the external diameter is 5.4 cm and the thickness of the pipe is 3 mm. Find the weight of the pipe, if 1 cm³ of lead mass is 25 grams. (Use π = 22/7 )

Convert all units to cm: Length (h) = 420 cm, R = 2.7 cm, r = (2.7 − 0.3) = 2.4 cm.

Using Volume of Hollow Cylinder = π × (R + r) × (R − r) × h

Volume = (22/7) × (2.7 + 2.4) × (2.7 − 2.4) × 420 = 22 × 60 × 5.1 × 0.3 = 2019.6 cm³.

Weight = (Volume × Density) / 1000 = (2019.6 × 25) / 1000 = 2019.6 / 40 = 50.49 kg.

**∴ The correct answer is 50.49 kg.**

⇒ Weight in kg = 50490 / 1000 = 50.49 kg

questions.question: In a school sports camp, there is food provision for 200 students for 30 days. If 50 more persons join the sports camp on the 2nd day, for how many days will the provision last?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Food provision = for 200 students × 30 days

On 2nd day, 50 more join → total = 250 students from day 2

**Formula used:**

Total food = Total persons × Total days

Remaining food = Initial food - food consumed on day 1

New duration = Remaining food ÷ New total persons

**Calculation:**

Total food = 200 × 30 = 6000 person-days

Food consumed on day 1 = 200 × 1 = 200

Remaining food = 6000 - 200 = 5800 person-days

From day 2, persons = 250

⇒ Remaining days = 5800 ÷ 250 = 23.2 days

Total days = 1 (already passed) + 23.2 = 24.2 days

**∴ The provision will last for approximately 24 days.**

questions.question: In the year of the coronation of Akbar, who among the following was designated as the Wakil of the Mughal kingdom with the title of 'Khan-i-Khanan'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bairam Khan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bairam Khan** was a trusted military commander and political advisor of Akbar, the third Mughal emperor of India.
 
• He was appointed as the **Wakil (Prime Minister)** of the Mughal Empire and given the title of **Khan-i-Khanan**, which means "Lord of Lords."
 
• During Akbar’s coronation in 1556, Bairam Khan played a key role in consolidating the Mughal rule and acted as the regent for the young emperor, who was only 13 years old at the time.
 
• Bairam Khan was instrumental in securing Akbar's throne by leading the Mughal forces to victory in the **Second Battle of Panipat (1556)** against Hemu, a powerful rival.
 
• As Wakil and Khan-i-Khanan, Bairam Khan managed the administrative and military affairs of the Mughal Empire during Akbar's early reign, ensuring stability and expansion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Khan-i-Khanan:**

 
 
• The title "Khan-i-Khanan" was one of the highest titles in the Mughal hierarchy, signifying supreme authority under the emperor.
 
• It was often bestowed upon individuals who demonstrated exceptional loyalty and administrative or military capabilities.
 
 
 
• **Bairam Khan’s Role in the Second Battle of Panipat (1556):**
 
 
• The Second Battle of Panipat was a decisive battle fought between the Mughal forces led by Bairam Khan and the army of Hemu, a Hindu general of the Sur Dynasty.
 
• Hemu was defeated, and this victory ensured the re-establishment of Mughal dominance in northern India.
 
 
 
• **Akbar’s Coronation:**
 
 
• Akbar was crowned as the Mughal emperor in 1556 at Kalanaur, Punjab, following the death of his father, Humayun.
 
• Since Akbar was a minor, Bairam Khan served as his regent, exercising significant authority on his behalf.
 
 
 
• **Bairam Khan’s Downfall:**
 
 
• In 1560, Akbar began asserting his independence and dismissed Bairam Khan from regency.
 
• Bairam Khan was later assassinated in Gujarat while traveling to Mecca for pilgrimage.

questions.question: Foods containing fats and carbohydrates are also called ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**energy giving foods**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Foods containing fats and carbohydrates are classified as **energy giving foods** because they provide the body with energy needed for daily activities.
 
• Carbohydrates are the **primary source of energy**, easily broken down into glucose, which fuels the body’s cells.
 
• Fats serve as a **concentrated energy reserve**, providing more than double the energy per gram compared to carbohydrates or proteins.
 
• Examples of energy giving foods include **bread, rice, potatoes (carbohydrates)**, and butter, nuts, and oils (fats).
 
• These foods are essential for maintaining the body’s metabolic functions, especially during physical exertion or intense activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carbohydrates:**

 
 
• Classified as simple (e.g., glucose, fructose) or complex (e.g., starch, fiber).
 
• Provide 4 calories per gram and are the body’s preferred energy source.
 
• Excess carbohydrates are stored as glycogen in the liver and muscles or converted to fat.
 
 
 
• **Fats:**
 
 
• Provide 9 calories per gram, making them the most calorie-dense nutrient.
 
• Include saturated fats (e.g., butter, lard) and unsaturated fats (e.g., olive oil, fish oil).
 
• Essential for absorption of fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, and K).
 
 
 
• **Energy Balance:**
 
 
• Maintaining energy balance is crucial for weight management and overall health.
 
• Excess energy intake leads to weight gain, while insufficient intake causes weight loss.
 
 
 
• **Other Energy Sources:**
 
 
• Proteins can also be used for energy, but primarily serve as building blocks for growth and repair.
 
• In cases of prolonged starvation, the body uses fats and proteins for energy.

• It is highly valued for its **scarcity, durability, and resistance to corrosion**, making it a preferred choice for jewelry and industrial applications.
 
• It is classified as a **noble metal** due to its excellent resistance to chemical reactions.
 
• Platinum is also extensively used in **automobile catalytic converters** to reduce harmful emissions and in various electronic and medical applications.
 
• Its rarity and high demand contribute to its significant economic value.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It is extensively used in electrical and electronic industries but is not classified as a precious mineral.

• It is not a precious mineral but is crucial in industrial applications.

questions.question: The Betul, Hoshangabad and Chhindwara districts of Madhya Pradesh is a part of which of the following Biosphere Reserves?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pachmarhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve is located in Madhya Pradesh and includes Betul, Hoshangabad, and Chhindwara districts.
 
• It was established in **1999** by the Government of India to conserve biodiversity and promote sustainable development.
 
• The Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve is a part of the Satpura range, which is known for its unique flora and fauna.
 
• This reserve is home to several endangered species, including the Indian giant squirrel and flying squirrel.
 
• Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve is also recognized under the UNESCO Man and Biosphere (MAB) Programme.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Biosphere Reserves in India:**

 
 
• Biosphere reserves are specially designated areas for the conservation of biodiversity, research, and sustainable development.
 
• India has **18 Biosphere Reserves**, including Nilgiri, Sundarbans, Gulf of Mannar, and Nanda Devi.
 
• Ten of these reserves are part of UNESCO’s World Network of Biosphere Reserves.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO Man and Biosphere Programme:**
 
 
• It is an intergovernmental scientific program launched in 1971 to improve the relationship between people and their environment.
 
• The program emphasizes sustainable development, conservation of biodiversity, and scientific research.
 
 
 
• **Satpura Range:**
 
 
• The Satpura range is a prominent mountain range in central India, spanning Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Chhattisgarh.
 
• It is rich in biodiversity, containing several forests, wildlife sanctuaries, and national parks.
 
 
 
• **Endangered Species in Pachmarhi Biosphere Reserve:**
 
 
• The reserve is home to endangered species like the Indian giant squirrel, leopard, and Indian pangolin.
 
• Efforts are made to protect these species and their habitats through conservation programs.

questions.question: Which of the following is the oldest dated forts in India, as first mentioned in Alexander the Great's war records, bringing it to the 4th century BCE?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kangra Fort**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kangra Fort** is considered one of the oldest forts in India, with its origins dating back to the **4th century BCE**.
 
• The fort was mentioned in the war records of **Alexander the Great**, indicating its historical significance during his invasion of India.
 
• Located in **Kangra, Himachal Pradesh**, the fort stands as an emblem of the **Trigarta Kingdom**, which was one of the oldest kingdoms in India.
 
• The fort has witnessed numerous invasions, including attacks by **Mahmud of Ghazni** in the 11th century and **Feroz Shah Tughlaq** in the 14th century.
 
• Its strategic location near the confluence of the **Banganga and Manjhi Rivers** made it a critical stronghold in ancient and medieval India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Trigarta Kingdom:**

 
 
• An ancient kingdom mentioned in the Mahabharata, it was known for its warrior clans and strategic location in the Himalayan region.
 
• The Kangra Fort was the capital of this kingdom, serving as a vital center of power.
 
 
 
• **Alexander’s Invasion of India:**
 
 
• Alexander the Great invaded India in 326 BCE, and his records provide valuable historical insights into the Indian subcontinent during that era.
 
• The mention of Kangra Fort in his war records highlights its prominence even during ancient times.
 
 
 
• **Architecture of Kangra Fort:**
 
 
• The fort is renowned for its massive stone walls and intricate gateways, showcasing ancient Indian military architecture.
 
• It houses temples and palaces, including the **Ambika Devi Temple**, reflecting its cultural and religious significance.
 
 
 
• **Other Ancient Forts in India:**
 
 
• **Gwalior Fort:** Known for its historical importance and architectural brilliance, but built later around the 6th century CE.
 
• **Kumbhalgarh Fort:** Constructed in the 15th century by Rana Kumbha in Rajasthan, famous for its massive walls.
 
• **Mehrangarh Fort:** Built in 1459 by Rao Jodha in Jodhpur, Rajasthan, it is one of the largest forts in India.

questions.question: Which of the following programmes is taken up by the Government of India for improvement of female literacy rates in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao (BBBP)** is a flagship program launched by the Government of India on **22 January 2015** at Panipat, Haryana.
 
• It aims to address gender discrimination and improve the declining **Child Sex Ratio (CSR)**, while also promoting education for girls.
 
• The program operates under the joint initiative of the **Ministry of Women and Child Development, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and Ministry of Education.**
 
• BBBP implements strategies focusing on **advocacy, community participation, and local-level interventions** to eliminate gender bias.
 
• The scheme has been instrumental in raising awareness about the importance of **female literacy, gender equality, and empowering girls** through education and social change.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Child Sex Ratio (CSR):**

 
 
• CSR refers to the number of girls per 1,000 boys in the age group of 0-6 years.
 
• India recorded a declining CSR over the years due to practices like female infanticide and prenatal sex determination.
 
• BBBP aims to reverse this trend through awareness campaigns and legal enforcement.
 
 
 
• **Components of BBBP:**
 
 
• **Advocacy campaigns** to promote awareness about gender equality and female education.
 
• **Multi-sectoral action:** Implementation at district levels through effective coordination among government departments.
 
• **Monitoring mechanisms:** Regular tracking of CSR and education-related indicators in targeted districts.
 
 
 
• **Government Interventions for Female Education:**
 
 
• Programs like **Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan** aim to provide universal access to elementary education.
 
• **Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya** focuses on improving access to education for girls from disadvantaged communities.
 
 
 
• **Legal Framework Supporting BBBP:**
 
 
• The **Pre-Conception and Pre-Natal Diagnostic Techniques (PCPNDT) Act, 1994**, prohibits sex-selective abortions.
 
• Government policies are also aligned with the **Right to Education Act, 2009**, ensuring free and compulsory education for children aged 6-14 years.

questions.question: As per the National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2021, which of the following groups of states is the poorest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the **National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021**, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and Jharkhand are among the poorest states in India.
 
• Bihar has the highest poverty rate in the country, with **51.91%** of its population classified as multidimensionally poor.
 
• Jharkhand follows Bihar with **42.16%** of its population living in multidimensional poverty.
 
• Uttar Pradesh is also among the poorest states, with **37.79%** of its population falling under the poverty index.
 
• The MPI measures poverty through three dimensions: **health, education, and standard of living**, encompassing 12 indicators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI):**

 
 
• It is developed by NITI Aayog in collaboration with the **Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI)** and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP).
 
• The MPI uses the **Global Multidimensional Poverty Index methodology** to assess poverty at the national level.
 
• The index includes three dimensions: **health, education, and standard of living**, with 12 indicators such as nutrition, child mortality, years of schooling, and access to cooking fuel, sanitation, and electricity.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index is published annually by OPHI and UNDP.
 
• India's performance in the global MPI influences its national policies and poverty alleviation programs.
 
 
 
• **Poverty Alleviation Programs in India:**
 
 
• Programs like the **Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana**, **National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme** (MGNREGA), and **National Food Security Act** aim to reduce poverty in the country.
 
• These programs focus on providing housing, employment, and food security to the poorest sections of society.
 
 
 
• **Regional Disparities:**

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of anaerobic activity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jumping**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Anaerobic activities** are high-intensity, short-duration exercises where the body relies on energy stored in muscles instead of oxygen.
 
• **Jumping** is a classic example of anaerobic activity because it requires quick bursts of energy without sustained oxygen supply.
 
• During jumping, muscles use **stored adenosine triphosphate (ATP)** and glycogen for energy production.
 
• Other examples of anaerobic activities include sprinting, weightlifting, and high-intensity interval training (HIIT).
 
• Anaerobic activities help improve **muscle strength, endurance, and power** while promoting fat loss and increasing metabolic rate.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Aerobic vs Anaerobic Activities:**

 
 
• **Aerobic activities** rely on oxygen for energy and are typically moderate-intensity, long-duration exercises (e.g., walking, swimming).
 
• **Anaerobic activities** are high-intensity, short-duration exercises that do not rely on oxygen (e.g., jumping, sprinting).
 
 
 
• **Energy Systems in Anaerobic Activity:**
 
 
• Anaerobic energy is provided by the **ATP-PC system** (phosphocreatine) and **anaerobic glycolysis**.
 
• These systems supply energy rapidly but for short durations (up to 2 minutes).
 
 
 
• **Benefits of Anaerobic Exercises:**
 
 
• Boosts muscle strength and power.
 
• Improves bone density and joint function.
 
• Increases metabolic rate, aiding in fat loss.
 
 
 
• **Risks and Precautions:**
 
 
• Anaerobic activities can strain muscles and joints if performed without proper warm-up or technique.
 
• Consult a fitness professional and avoid overtraining to prevent injuries.

questions.question:
Select the correct order of processes used for water purification in waterworks.

1. Filtration

2. Chlorination

3. Suspended impurity sedimentation

4. Solid impurity sedimentation
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4-3-1-2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The correct sequence for water purification in waterworks is: **solid impurity sedimentation → suspended impurity sedimentation → filtration → chlorination**.
 
• **Solid impurity sedimentation**: Involves allowing larger particles and debris to settle at the bottom of the tank.
 
• **Suspended impurity sedimentation**: Addition of coagulants like alum helps smaller particles clump together and settle.
 
• **Filtration**: Water passes through sand, gravel, and other filter media to remove fine particles and impurities.
 
• **Chlorination**: Disinfection by adding chlorine to eliminate harmful microorganisms and pathogens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Coagulation and Flocculation**:

 
 
• These are essential processes where chemicals like alum are added to water to aggregate suspended particles into larger flocs.
 
• Flocs settle faster during sedimentation, improving water clarity.
 
 
 
• **Chlorination**:
 
 
• A widely used disinfection technique in water treatment plants.
 
• It effectively kills bacteria, viruses, and other microbes, ensuring safe drinking water.
 
 
 
• **Filtration Media**:
 
 
• Common filtration materials include sand, gravel, and activated carbon.
 
• These materials help in trapping fine particles and adsorbing organic impurities.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Sedimentation**:
 
 
• Reduces the load on downstream filtration systems by removing large and suspended impurities early in the process.
 
• Enhances the efficiency of the entire water purification process.

questions.question: What is the standard length of a cricket pitch?

• A cricket pitch is a rectangular area located at the center of the field, measuring precisely **22 yards (20.12 meters) in length and 10 feet (3.05 meters) in width.**
 
• The pitch is used for bowling, batting, and running between the wickets during play.
 
• The length of 22 yards is internationally standardized by the **International Cricket Council (ICC).**
 
• The stumps are set at each end of the pitch, and the popping creases are marked 4 feet in front of the stumps.
 
• The pitch's dimensions have remained consistent since the early development of cricket in England in the 17th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Crease:** Lines drawn on the pitch to define areas for the bowler and batsman.
 
• **Wicket:** Consists of three stumps and two bails, placed at each end of the pitch.
 
• **Popping Crease:** The line a batsman must reach to avoid being run out.
 
• **Bowling Crease:** The line where the stumps are placed.
 
 
 
• **Pitch Conditions:**
 
 
• Pitches can vary in nature—**flat pitches favor batsmen**, while grassy or cracked pitches benefit bowlers.
 
• In Test cricket, pitch conditions change significantly over five days, affecting gameplay.
 
 
 
• **Historical Development:**
 
 
• The 22-yard measurement has been in place since cricket's codification in the 18th century.
 
• It was derived from the traditional English unit of measurement called "chain," which equals 22 yards.
 
 
 
• **Role of ICC:**
 
 
• The ICC regulates pitch preparation to ensure consistency and fairness in international matches.
 
• Pitch inspections are conducted to avoid undue advantages for either batsmen or bowlers.
